status_effects.explanation: Her jealous possessiveness of social capital and self-serving version of events locally expose her vanity and hypocrisy.
His blushing omission and retaliatory judgment of his questioner reveal a comparable petty vanity and dishonesty.
The narrator moves from being left out (formerly alone at the Champs-Élysées when Gilberte departed) to being actively included in the Swann household's outings.

appraisal_events.evidence: Mme Bontemps eût souhaité qu'après elle personne de son monde à elle ne fût présenté à la princesse. ... les pelés qu'à la fin elle accusait de s'être invités eux-mêmes ... c'était les Cottard.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator satirizes Mme Bontemps' jealous possessiveness over her exclusive acquaintance with the duchesse de Vendôme and her self-serving retelling of the dinner that diminishes the Cottards' presence.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Je les oubliais », avait en rougissant répondu Cottard au maladroit qu'il classa désormais dans la catégorie des mauvaises langues.
appraisal_events.explanation: Cottard is caught blushing after conveniently omitting the Bontemps from his self-flattering account of the dinner, then vindictively brands the person who exposed him a gossip, exposing his own vanity.

appraisal_events.evidence: ces sorties maintenant M. et Odette m'y admettaient, j'avais une place dans leur landau et même c'était à moi qu'on demandait si j'aimais mieux aller...
appraisal_events.explanation: Swann and Odette now actively include the narrator in family outings that had once excluded him, giving him a seat in their carriage and consulting his preferences, staging him as an included participant.
